To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lubricant depletion characteristics induced by laser heating in TAMR systems are largely dependent on lubricant film thickness, and that the DLC thin film on the disk surface is also affected by laser heating.
the lubricant film is depleted by laser heating and that the depletion mechanism is different for thin and thick lubricant films.

the lubricant depletion characteristics due to laser heating depend on lubricant film thickness, that lubricant depletion occurs predominantly via lubricant evaporation, that the lubricant film on the disk surface changes in reflectivity due to rapid laser irradiation, and that the DLC thin films on the surfaces of disk substrates are affected by rapid laser irradiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the lubricant depletion characteristics induced by rapid laser heating in the TAMR system.
the fundamental understanding of the lubricant depletion mechanism in the TAMR system.
lubricant depletion and DLC damage due to rapid laser irradiation in TAMR systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lubricant depletion due rapid laser heating is predominantly caused by lubricant evaporation and that the reflectivity change of the DLC film is due to the density decrease of the film.
the lubricant depletion characteristics induced by rapid laser heating are largely dependent on the lubricant type and thickness.
the effects of lubricant depletion on the lubrication characteristics of the disk surfaces are strongly dependent on both the lubricant film and DLC thin-film thicknesses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lubricant depletion mechanism in TAMR depends largely on the lubricant thickness and the laser irradiation duration.
the lubricant depletion and the DLC damage characteristics due to rapid laser irradiation should be considered for the development of practical TAMR systems.
the fundamental research conducted in this study will be beneficial in developing TAMR systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have clarified the lubricant depletion mechanisms and the damage to the DLC thin films induced by rapid laser heating in TAMR systems.

the lubricant film should be thicker than one monolayers in order to prevent lubricant depletion in actual TAMR systems, and the lubricant should be selected to have a low evaporation temperature in order to minimize the lubricant depletion due evaporation.
we have elucidated the fundamental mechanisms of lubricant depletion in TAMR systems, and we have proposed a new approach for reducing lubricant depletion.
